You are interested in quantifying the amount of **formic acid** in indoor air. To do this, you employ the use of a passive sampler made with KOH (a strong base), that transform the formic acid into its conjugate base, **formate** (HCOO$^-$). You quantify the amount of formate in your passive sampler via ion chromatography coupled with a conductivity detector, after extraction of the passive sampler into water.

## Section 1: Experimental set-up (16 points)

**Nine** passive tube-type samplers are made using KOH dispersed on 5 mm metal discs secured at the end of a 5 cm quartz tube, which are enough for experiments, method blanks, and zeros in *triplicate*.**Three** samplers were made without KOH to serve as an experimental control.

A graphic of the tube is included below:

![KOH sampler](Solid%20KOH.png)

Samplers were deployed for 4 hours before extraction into 5 mL of milliQ water. Each sample was measured via IC-CD and the peak areas of all the extracts is included in "Assignment2.csv"

#### 7b) Based on the mass of formate collected on the passive samplers, calculate the concentration of formic acid (in µg/cm$^3$) in indoor air, with its uncertainty. (20 points)

The concentration of the analyte in air is described by the following equation: $$ C = \frac{M \times L}{D \times A \times t} $$

Where M is the mass of formate collected from ambient air, L is the length of the sampling tube, D is the diffusion coefficient of formic acid (0.153 cm$^2$/s), A is the area of sample collection, and t is collection time.
